one should mark out the outer maṇḍala, inlaid with vajra-jewels.
verse [§ -niryūha-], verse on *ni* + *ūha*
Within that very [mandala] is an eight-petaled lotus with filaments;
its exterior is encircled by a garland of vajras, radiating forth as an emanation of a multitude of Buddhas.
verse § lotus], lotus verse
One should draw an eight-spoked wheel, the abode of all accomplishments and qualities;
on the outside, it is called by the name Khecarī, consisting of a row of black thunderbolts.
The eight-spoked wheel of Bhūcarī is encircled by a row of lotus pillars.
The circle of those dwelling in the netherworld (pātāla) is well-encircled by a series of wheels.
The yogi, composed in meditative absorption, should draw wheels and vajras at the junctions of the spokes.
Likewise, one should likewise [visualize] a line of flames extending as far as the Cakravāḍa mountains.
At the intervals between the spokes, the yogi in meditative equipoise should draw vajras; likewise, up to the edge of the wheel’s rim, there should be blazing lines. 495.
The great yogin Śrūheruka, stationed in the center of the wheel-ground, should then divide the doors with the wrathful gaze of the syllable HĪḤ. (496)
The great yogin Heruka Śrī, having settled well in the center of the wheel, shall then open the gates with a wrathful gaze while uttering the syllable *hiḥ*. 496.
The gate is considered to be one-eighth of the wheel's diameter and is to be devoid of a railing;
a wise person should have the turret made according to the measurement of the gate.
The doors are one-eighth the size of the wheel, and the cornices are wide. The door-frames and the dimensions of the doors, as well as the divine panels, are likewise. 497.

The altar (vedī) is half the width of the door on all sides; likewise are the cheeks (kapola), the side-panels (pakṣaka), the necklaces (hāra), half-necklaces (ardhahāra), the moon and sun, the bands (paṭṭa), the garlands (sraj), and the friezes (paṭṭikā). || 498 ||
The archways are adorned on all sides with half-arches, side-posts, and panels; likewise, they are decorated with lattices, half-lattices, suns, moons, canopies, and garlands of flowers. 498.
The ground for the colored powders (rajobhūmi) outside the area of the root-line (mūlasūtra) is half that size;
the ground for the lines of the vajra-pillars and so forth is equal to the ground for the colored powders. (499)
The area for the colors is half of that; the area behind the ground [for the pillars] is according to the root line.
The area for the pillars, such as the vajra-pillars and so forth, is equal to the area for the colors. 499.
The archway (toraṇa) should be three times the width of the door and provided with banners and bells;
from the outer corners, banners are raised by the wind together with the bells.
The archways are three times the size of the gates; they are adorned with banners and bells, and the banners are moved by the wind at the outer corners. 500.
In the middle of the Brahma-thread and so forth, one should cause four threads to be laid out;
the lotus-wheel is to be made within the wheels of mind, speech, and body.
Within the middle of the [lotus] petals, the wise one should draw five circular lines;
another four lines should be made in the form of a vajra-garland and so forth. 502.
*... At the beginning, the yogi should cast the chalk-line, and within that, the knowledge-line, according to the ritual procedure, maintaining equality in all directions.* 503.
First is the line of space; beneath that is the line of gnosis.
Having traversed all directions with equality, the yogi should strike them according to the ritual procedure. 503.
The supreme Heruka should delineate the outer mandala in both direct and reverse order; in that very same way, he should delineate the inner body. 504.
By this [method of] proceeding in order and reversing the order, this is the line for the outer maṇḍala;
likewise, it is the inner nature of the body. 504.
O Lord, that which is produced by the causal complex (sāmagrī) should delineate the maṇḍala of the body—innate, pure by its very nature, and joined with the heroes and heroines. 505.
Coemergent and pure by nature, the Lord of Heroes and Heroines, the Protector arisen from the assembly—by him the mandala of the body shall be marked with lines. 505.
The procedure for laying out the lines for the external and internal [mandalas]. o || 7 ||
This is the ritual for laying out the outer and inner lines. Closer 7.
Having taken a bone from a cremation ground together with ashes and a brick, one should paint the Heruka-vajra joined with yellow orpiment. || 506 ||
Having properly gathered bones from a charnel ground, together with ashes, leaves, brick-dust, and human fat, one should skillfully draw the wheel of Heruka. 506.

Having placed the dust upon the skull according to the procedure stated in the Sūtra, the wise one, gazing with a blazing look, draws that [dust] which has entered the heart of the wheel of knowledge (jñānacakra). || 507 ||
Having placed the colored powders upon the crown of the head, the wise one should perform the rite of drawing the lines.
Having summoned [the deities] with the blazing navel, one should insert the essence of the wisdom-wheel. 507.
And having consecrated it with the mantra of the Ḍākinī of all Buddhas.
Śrī Heruka himself, the King, is situated within the wheel. || 508 ||
Highly praised by the secret mantras of the ḍākinīs of all the Buddhas, may the glorious Heruka, the sovereign lord, be well-established in the center of the wheel. 508.
This earth, filled with all cremation grounds, is the supreme seal of the Lord;
one should perform the scattering of dust for the twenty-fourfold division.
All those born from the charnel grounds are the mudrās of the Supreme Īśvara.
One should begin the drawing of the colored powder mandala according to the twenty-fourfold division. 509.
With his left hand, the wise one, moving counter-clockwise toward the southeast, [should place the colors]:
white, yellow, red, green, and black.
With the left hand, the wise one should circumambulate from the direction of the fire;
likewise white, yellow, red, and green. 510.
Accompanied by the four goddesses and surrounded by the four heroes,
one should draw five pure lines with an interval of the measure of a barley grain between them.
Endowed with the four goddesses and surrounded by the four heroes, one should draw five lines of pure measurement within the intermediate space. 511.
And so it has been said:
"One should draw the lines exactly as they were taught, with each line being one-twentieth part of the door."
If there is a coarse fall, disease will occur; through cultivation, there will be loss of wealth. || 512 ||
One should draw [the design] with equal joy in twenty parts of the door;
through meditation, illness will arise, and by means of the subtle, wealth will be exhausted. 512.
Through a curved [line], there is enmity; through a severed one, death between teacher and disciple;
by the falling of a clockwise-turning [line], there shall be the pinning down of the dusts. || 513 ||
Through impurity, there is aversion; through punishment, both teacher and disciple die.
By drawing [the mandala] while circumambulating to the right, the colored powders will become powerless. 513.
The southern [direction] should be drawn black, the eastern dark-brown, the northern red, and the western yellow; these beautiful [colors] should be depicted by those who know the mantras. (514)
The southern ground is black, the eastern green, likewise the northern red, and the western ground is drawn yellow; [thus] it becomes pleasing through the stages of secret mantra. 514.
However, for the petals of the middle dharma-circle, the visualization should be performed according to the colors of the directions within the Heruka maṇḍala, which arises from the Yoginīcakra. 515.
In the center, the petals of the lotus should be visualized according to the colors of the directions;
thus arises the wheel of yoginīs, and the maṇḍala of Heruka is formed. 515.
One should draw the wheels of mind, speech, and body as blue, red, and great white respectively;
all other elements outside the arches should be drawn according to what is aesthetically pleasing.
Large blue, red, and white [circles] are the wheels of mind, speech, and body;
all other parts should be painted as beautifully as possible on the outer archways. 516.
One should place the Hero (Vīra), accompanied by Mahādevī, upon the pericarp;
and Herukavajra, joined with Ḍākinī and the others, upon the petals.
The Hero, together with the Great Goddess, should be placed at the navel;
the Ḍākinīs and others are perfectly arrayed upon the petals of the Heruka-vajra. 517.
The mantrin, composed in meditation, should draw the goddesses beginning with Kākāsyā, joined with the illustrious Heruka, at the gates and in the corner sections. 518.

Likewise, the goddesses such as Cāmuṇḍī and the others, together with Heruka and the rest, should be drawn by the mantra-practitioner in meditative equipoise at the gates and intermediate points. 518.
Likewise, outside is the abode of the pretas, joined by hosts of rākṣasas and others;
and above the gateway is a thunderbolt, formidable with flickering flames.
Likewise, in that outer realm of pretas, there are those such as rākṣasīs;
above the vajra archway, rays of light radiate and the mouth is wide open. 519.
The outer maṇḍala has been described as adorned with the falling of colored powders;
however, the inner [maṇḍala] should be understood by the wise one through the instruction of the Guru. 520.
The outer maṇḍala, beautiful with the arrangement of colored powders, has been taught;
the wise one who has pleased the guru should understand the inner nature. 520.
Through the yoga of the inconceivable form, one who has transcended the realm of passion is purified;
with a joyful mind, he causes [the disciple] to fall through the play of innate bliss. 521.
Through inconceivable application, it is a fault to draw the colored powder;
through the play of innate joy, one should draw oneself with a mind of austerity. 521.
When beginning the mandala and other rites, if winds and so forth arise, one should ward off all malevolent forces through the yoga of identifying oneself with Śrī Heruka. 522.

When the winds and other elements arise at the commencement of the mandala and so forth, one should clear away all malevolent influences through the application of the glorious Heruka as oneself. 522.
The procedure for removing external and internal impurities. o || End of section 8 ||
This is the ritual for spreading the outer and inner colored powders. Section 8.
The cry "Pukāra" is said to be the first; those auspicious syllables which are in the spokes, one should bring their wheel of knowledge together with the rays. 523.
Those primordial wisdoms of this [deity], whatever their excellent colors on the spokes, summon the wheel of wisdom into equipoise by means of the light rays of that meditative concentration. 523.
It is adorned by numerous hosts of goddesses and by bodhisattvas of great supernatural power,
as well as by other heroes of great strength who are like the finest jewels of reality.
Together with many hosts of goddesses and bodhisattvas of great miraculous power, adorned with the jewels of reality itself, and other heroes of great strength. 524.
The wise one should always worship that wheel according to the procedure taught in the tantra;
or else, it is the procedure for worship of all the tantras, beginning with those of the Buddhas. (525)

The wise one, through the ritual procedures arising from his own continuous stream of being, or else through the ritual of worship from the *Sarvabuddha* [Tantra] and so forth, shall please Cakrasaṃvara. 525.
White, yellow, red, green, and black—
this is the flower-seal (puṣpamudrā) when anointed, [offering] festivals of the five qualities of sensual pleasure.
White, yellow, and likewise red, green and black itself—these flowers, as a single mudrā, are the very nature of the five qualities of desire. 526.
When worshipped, the five white seals, colored with the five hues of lac, turmeric, blue, and fierce [pigments], are equally accomplished.
With the supreme excellence of saffron and the imitation of the five colors, it expands with the nature of the five whites; through equal offering, accomplishment will be attained. 527.
Whether consisting of all the elements or likewise consisting of the root of life,
its manifold variety and fragrance are accomplished equally as before.
The nature of all the elements, as well as the nature of the life-force and the channels, will be established in equilibrium, endowed with various diverse fragrances, just as before. 528.
Two types of sandalwood, clay, musk, camphor, and the nail of the sallakī—incense combined with jaggery accomplishes all rites. || 529 ||
The two types of sandalwood, mṛgamada, and saffron, along with śāla and nagakesara incense mixed with sugar—these perfumes and so forth accomplish all ritual activities. 529.
Gandha, guggulu, sarja, camphor, and musk—by means of these substances, one should cook oil for a lamp that increases the light. (530)
Guggulu, sa-rdza-ra, and guggula, as well as fragrances derived from wild animals—these substances should be used to prepare an illumination with fabricated ghee. 530.
Having mixed sandalwood, saffron, camphor, and musk, the perfected Vāmamudrā, dressed in fine garments, is fumigated and cooked. 531.

Sandalwood, agallochum, priyaṅgu, and campaka; perfumes born from mountains and wild game, as well as cloths produced from artificial and poisonous substances—these are the cloths of excellent mudrās. 531.
Kakkola, elaka, mustaka, camphor, and musk—these, finely ground, one should place as a pill within a khadira vessel. (532)
Kakkola, elā, mustaka, guggulu, and the scent derived from deer— having finely ground these together, one should place them in a hollow of khadira wood. 532.
Cinnamon bark, cinnamon leaves, lodhra, black pepper, and camphor constitute *prativedhana*; the obstruction caused by mango oil is known as *mukhavāma*. || 533 ||
One should thoroughly employ the leaves of *twa ga*, *lo dha*, *ma ri tsa*, and *ga pur*. It is remembered that [this] is to be applied to the mouth with the oil of *sahākāri*. 533.
Then one should present the offering of the bali-oblation. || 534 ||
Thereafter, offer the torma offering. 534.
Vilāsinī, Pramadā, Madana, Amṛta, as well as Ekavīra, Kharakāmuka, and Viṭa; likewise,
the Lacanā and other rasas are like sugar and other substances that resemble nectar.
The accomplishment of the essence of all selves is achieved completely and without exception. || 536 ||
Fermented liquor that has not been altered, liquor, and likewise nectar;
the *ekavīra* grain, *yava*, *gavedhuka*, *biṭa*, and *śiteṭi* are likewise so.
All flavors such as salt and the like, and substances such as sugar, are similar to nectar.
Through the essence of all things, one accomplishes the siddhis without exception or remainder. 535–536.
When various foods, prepared together with wine and meat, are provided—being delightful through the enjoyment of beloved ones—the supreme lifespan is successfully attained. (537)

Through the display of manifold manifestations, the siddhi is attained; through the perfect union of liquor and meat, the enjoyment of desires and the supreme, great fortune are fully accomplished. 537.
The ripe amṛta-panasa, the grape, the coconut, and the āruka—this is the fruit of the udaya, which brings about an internal festival of all the fruits of accomplishment. 538.
The fruit of the *pākava* tree, the *guḍūcī* grain, the *naḷikā*, the *āluka*, and so forth—this mudrā of fruits is eternally projected as the fruit of all accomplishments. 538.
One should smear the mango stone with a paste of sugar and honey,
and then treat it with saffron oil and other fragrant substances.
Apply a paste made from mixing with śarkara; apply it to mango stones.
The essence of sahakāra oil and so forth becomes a perfectly balanced fragrance. 539.
Having dyed it with turmeric and, as appropriate, with bark and other such substances,
one should offer it at the time of worship.
Having cooked the outer husks and so forth with *ba bla* and lacquer according to what is appropriate, one should offer them at the time of worship. 540.
The external worship has been indicated by me as being accompanied by that which is born of the body;
having performed the worship and satisfied [the deities], one should go outside and cast the bali offering.
Fully endowed with the arising of the body, I have taught the outer offerings;
having properly honored and pleased [the deities], go outside and present the bali offering. 540.
Having become naked with disheveled hair and standing leaning upon a khaṭvāṅga staff,
one should offer liquor and meat to the ḍākinīs and others.
Naked, with hair disheveled, and properly holding a khaṭvāṅga, one should offer [the substance] thoroughly combined with alcohol and meat to the ḍākinīs and others. 541.
Furthermore, the wise one should perform the great yoga of emanation and so forth, facing south and situated in a high place. (542)
Having abandoned [places such as] Byang-gnas and other sites favored by great yogins, the wise one should face toward the south and reside in a high location. 542.
Having stepped upon the right foot with the left, one should gaze upward;
joined with the *jvālāmudrā*, it consists of the utterance of the syllable *phet*.
Pressing down the right foot with the left, looking upward, perfectly endowed with the blazing mudrā, and possessing the nature of uttering the syllable *pheṃ*. 543.
Oṃ āralli hoḥ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ || Mantra 57 ||
oṃ ara lli ho dzāḥ hūṃ baṃ hoḥ || Mantra 57 ||
Oṃ, you are the pledge of the Vajra-Ḍākinīs; behold! Hoḥ! (Mantra 58)
Oṃ vajraḍākinī samayas tvaṃ dṛśya hoḥ. Mantra 58.
Having first recited the mantra once, five times, and likewise seven times, one should contemplate [the substance] placed in a skull-cup, conjoined with the *samaya* and *phalgu* [liquids]. (544)
One, five, and seven times, one should first recite the mantra; endowed with the substances of the samaya, one should visualize them within the skull-cup. 544.
The *vajrāñjali* with the hands opened upward is known as the *āvali-mudrā*;
it shall please all the heroes and heroines who abide upon the path. (545)
The vajra palms are opened upward; this is renowned as the garland mudrā.
It pleases all the lords of heroes and heroines who abide upon the path. 545.
With a concentrated mind, one should offer the bali-oblation to the guardians of the directions, the pretas, and the bhūtas,
using these mantras ending with "khakhāṭyai," which assist in the attainment of all siddhis.
Having purified the directions and entered meditative equipoise, one should offer the *bali* to the pretas and elemental spirits;
by means of this mantra beginning with "Kha kha," all desires are accomplished. 546.

Oṃ kha kha khāhi khāhi! O all you yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, unmādas, apasmāras, ḍākinīs, and so forth: accept this bali offering! Guard the pledge! Bestow all accomplishments! Eat and drink as much as you desire, according to your pleasure! Do not transgress! Be my companions in every way for the sake of true happiness and purification! Hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā! (Mantra 59)

Oṃ kha kha khā hi khā hi | All you yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, those possessed by madness, those with epilepsy, vajra-ḍākinīs, and so forth—accept this bali! Grant me all accomplishments! Come! Go! Be established! Move about! May all my intentions be fulfilled! Be purified! May they abide together! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! (Mantra 59)

Having offered the bali-oblation, the mantra-practitioner, endowed with compassion, power, and yoga, and joined by the hero and the mistress of heroes, should then perform the consumption of the sacrificial porridge (caru).
Having offered the *bali* cake, thereafter the mantra-practitioner should begin the consumption of food and drink:
"Endowed with the sovereignty of heroes and heroines, and possessing the application of the power of compassion. (547)

He has the form of a wrathful deity marked by a vajra, with a wide-open face of subjugation and the head adorned with a crescent moon; he is beautiful, with a multitude of hanging banners fashioned from the ringing sounds of bells,
his fierce hair tied upward and matted together, and he is decorated with various flowers bound into garlands.
The Vajrayoginī should hold a flaming khaṭvāṅga, which produces excellent delight. 548.
Marked with vajras and possessing the form of a wrathful deity, their gaping mouths are bound at the crown by crescent moons;
they are beautified by the sound of lovely bells and possess a multitude of various fluttering banners.
Adorned with fierce sounds and many diverse flowers, they wear bound garlands.
The vajra-yogin should grasp Kha-twāṅ-ga, which blazes and generates supreme joy. 548.

Having prostrated to the illustrious Vajradevī, and thereafter to the excellent Guru Heruka, the Lord of the Mandala, he should gather the most eminent disciples endowed with the qualities of great warriors and all the various special offerings;
then, his essence being the bliss of the stainless *hūṃ* syllable, he should strike the hand-drum (*ḍamaruka*) with his right hand.
Performing the play of the Ācārya, he enters the center of the maṇḍala hall with certainty. || 549 ||

Having prostrated to the glorious Vajradevī, the supreme Guru, and Heruka with his retinue and protectors, and having accepted the various offerings from the excellent disciple endowed with supreme qualities,
[he plays] the fine ḍamaru drum on the right, resounding the stainless *hūṃ*, the pinnacle of joy.
The master Rolpa Dzad (Līlāvatī) definitely enters into the center of the mandala house. 549 ||
One should cause the southern door to be opened and the remaining doors to be bolted;
this is declared according to the sequence of the Devītantra by one who knows the Yogatantras, beginning with the east.
Having gone to the southern gate, one should circumambulate the remaining [gates].
This is the sequence of the goddesses' tantras; the Yoga Tantras belong to the eastern direction and so forth. 551.
One should cause [the practitioner] to enter through the southern gate, as stated by Bhūtavādin;
this should be understood as being for the sake of conventional truth, involving conceptual construction in the painted maṇḍala.
As for proceeding to the southern gate: one should understand that the examination of the mandala to be drawn, which was taught as being well-spoken, is for the sake of conventional truth. 552.
There is no conceptualization of "east" and so forth through a division of the directions' limits;
rather, that which is the face of the yogi who is so agreed upon is itself considered the east.
When directions such as the south are conceptually imputed through their infinite parts, what indeed is that which is called the "southern face"? This is merely conventional for the yogi. (553)
First, having established the protection wheel (*rakṣācakra*) and performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six heroic deities according to the dharma rites with the mantras,
Then one should accomplish the mandala. First, one should construct the protective wheel with the arrangement of the six heroes and goddesses;
thereafter, one should accomplish the mandala through the ritual of consecrating it with mantras.
Seated comfortably with effort regarding the posture upon the pedestal of the limbs of wisdom, in the center of the mandala ground, endowed with the previously described characteristics. (555)
With effort upon a comfortable seat, on top of the seat of the branches of wisdom, in the center of the mandala ground, possessing the characteristics previously explained. 555.
One should scatter the substance upon the maṇḍala, beautiful with jewels and gold, combined with great *phalgu* fruit, and well-perfumed in eight places. || 556 ||
All beautiful gold and jewels should be scattered upon the maṇḍala; it should be well-incensed at the eight locations with great quantities of meat. 556.
One should offer a hundred lamps filled with abundant oil,
strewn with various flowers and made fragrant with various perfumes.
One should offer eight lamps filled with abundant sesame oil, beautifully arranged with various flowers and well-perfumed with diverse fragrances. 557.
At the four gates are the four heroes, with two yoginīs stationed at each;
they possess bodies adorned with the five mudrās and are decorated with five crests. || 558 ||
At the four gates dwell heroes and yoginīs in non-dual union;
the body is marked with the five mudrās and so forth, and is characterized by five heads. 558.
Some were naked while others were clothed; all were reeling with the joy of wine, wearing crests of matted hair, and intent upon consuming sacrificial porridge.
Some wear the garments of the naked ascetics, while others are intoxicated with the joy of wine;
all are adorned with crested headdresses, and they strive intensely for their food and drink. 559.
In the other corner regions, they are joined by Vīra and Vīreśvarī;
embracing the vajra and bell, they are eager to press against each other’s breasts. (560)
In the other intermediate directions are the heroes and heroines endowed with mastery; they embrace one another with vajras and bells, intent on pressing their breasts. 560.
The illustrious leader of the host stands like a universal monarch,
joined by the four goddesses and kissing the face of Vārāhī.
The lord of the hosts of gaṇas is the glorious Cakravartin, well-established;
he is perfectly joined with four goddesses and kisses the face of Vārāhī. 561.
Some yogins sing songs, some dance,
and some, eager for the consumption of sacrificial porridge, engage in laughter.
Some sing songs, some perform dances, O yogi;
some indulge in laughter, being attached to food and conduct. (562)
Some play musical instruments, while some are reciters of auspicious verses;
they worship the Great Hero, the Lord of Cakrasaṃvara. || 563 ||
With the beating of various drums and with diverse auspicious songs, they worship the great hero Cakrasaṃvara, the blissful one. 563.
All are joined with the six heroes, adorned by the yoginīs, and endowed with the armor and other [protections], abiding in the vajra-maṇḍala. (564)
All are endowed with the six heroes; adorned with yoginīs, and perfectly equipped with armor and the like, they dwell well within the vajra maṇḍala. 564.
Having thus armored oneself so as to be impenetrable even by the thirty-three gods, one should cause the festival of Heruka to begin with the consumption of sacrificial porridge (caru). 565.
Thus, having donned the armor, one is indestructible even by the gods of the Thirty-three;
having generated enthusiasm for Heruka, one should properly undertake the eating and the feast offering. 565.
The ritual procedure for the worship of the external and internal maṇḍala deities, heroes, and heroines. o || 9 ||
This is the ritual for making offerings to the deities of the outer and inner mandalas, as well as to the heroes (vīra) and the sovereign goddesses (īśvarī). Closer 9.
Once the wheel of commitment (samayacakra) has been accomplished, one should bring in the wheel of gnosis (jñānacakra),
enclosing it with the mind by means of upward glances.
The sixth wheel of the commitment (samaya-cakra) is perfectly endowed with the wheel of gnosis (jñāna-cakra); having performed the union with the mind, one gazes upward. 566.
Through the application of the mantras and the *phetkāra* sound, together with the mudrās of the previous invocation,
the goddesses dwelling in infinite regions become joyful and bestow spiritual accomplishments (*siddhi*).

By first inviting [the deities] and forming the mudrās, and by employing the recitation of mantras and the sound of "pheṃ," the deities residing in the infinite directions are pleased and bestow the siddhis. 567.
Accompanied by heroes and heroines, adorned with their respective primary signs and so forth, the perfectly awakened ones, the compassionate lords of the world, arrive. (568)
The Hero, the Sovereign of Heroes and Heroines, adorned with the signs of his former vows and other marks—the compassionate Protector of the World, the Perfect Buddha—is about to depart. 568.
Arising from the cultivation of non-duality within the mandala, the abode of Heruka, they undoubtedly bring about the delightful state of empowerment. || 569 ||
One attains the siddhi of non-duality; there is no doubt that the mandala of Heruka’s realm will bring about the delightful state of blessings. 569.
The procedure for the invocation of the wheel of knowledge regarding the external and internal. || o || End of section 10.
This is the ritual for inviting the outer and inner wheels of primordial wisdom. Closer 10.
Having worshipped the yoginīs of the wheel with both external and internal mind, [one should worship] those situated in the central and other locations with the flower of self-arisen bliss. (570)
With the outer and inner mind, one worships the wheel of yoginīs;
the self-arisen mountain flowers themselves dwell perfectly in the abodes of the sons and so forth. 570.
Having washed it comfortably with that [water], and having consecrated the others situated upon the wheel by means of the non-dual mantra, || 571 ||
Having smeared his face with that, he who dwells in another mandala consecrates it, having highly praised it with the mantra of non-duality and the absence of duality. 571.
Having empowered each door with the secret mantras of the ḍākinīs, the practitioner, composed in meditation, should perform one hundred and eight recitations. 572.

With the secret mantra of the ḍākinīs, one should consecrate each and every door; the supreme recitation of eight hundred times should be performed by the mantrin himself while in meditative equipoise. 572.
Afterwards, one should recite the *ālikāli* for the sake of consecration within the mandala;
the goddess is formidable, abounding in the absence of fear, terrible, and of beautiful form. (573)
Having recited the *ālikāli*, one subsequently consecrates the maṇḍala;
amidst many terrifying sounds, there are the beautiful bodies of the terrifying goddesses. 573.
In the five houses, those excellent goddesses come and stand before one;
they bestow vast accomplishment upon the practitioner, of this there is no doubt. (574)
The supreme goddess of the five houses, having arrived, sits before him; she will undoubtedly bestow vast accomplishments upon the practitioner. 574.
And so it has been said:
"Likewise, it is taught:
'The shedding of tears while dancing, as well as eating and self-emergence.'"
One should perform the non-transgression of the vajra, as well as worship while naked. || 575 ||
He shall constantly shed tears; likewise, he shall subsist on food produced from his own body.
He shall not step upon a vajra, and he shall likewise perform worship while remaining naked. 575.
This is the sequence for the group of mudrās of all the Vāmeśvarīs:
once the *caru* has been prepared and consumed, they seize the practitioner by the throat.
Through all the powers of the left, this sequence of the assembly of mudrās is perfectly accomplished by means of eating and enjoyment; the practitioner who holds the throat well [attains it]. 576.
Those yoginīs go to their own abodes, delighted with him who desires accomplishment;
the mantra-practitioner, possessing the power of great supernatural attainments, becomes like Heruka. || 577 ||
Having gone to his own abode, he is pleased; the yoginīs desire his accomplishment.
The mantrin who has realized great miraculous power is born as the supreme Heruka. 577.

Alternatively, having become Heruka, the accomplisher of all desired aims, he sports within the wheel of the sky-farers (khecarī), accompanied by the earth-dwellers (bhūcarī) and the others. || 578 ||
Alternatively, being endowed with the celestial wheel of Khecarī, the terrestrial [wheel], and so forth, and having become the compassionate Heruka, one accomplishes all desired aims. 578.
The glorious one shall wander through the buddha-fields, honored by all the buddhas;
or else, due to a lack of merit, he may not attain accomplishment while remaining within the maṇḍala. (579)

Having circumambulated the glorious buddha-fields, one will be honored by all the buddhas; otherwise, due to a deficiency in merit, if the abiding of the mandala is not accomplished, [the result will be as follows]. 579.

Being solely intent on the welfare of sentient beings, one should begin the consumption of the sacrificial porridge (caru), even while engaged in laughter and dance, or devoted to song and dance. 580.
Exclusively striving for the benefit of sentient beings, they engage in eating and conduct;
endowed with laughter, grace, and so forth, they find delight in song and dance. 580.
The mantra-practitioner should worship the heroes and yoginīs with various kinds of food;
[he should perform] the gestures, dramatic postures, and so forth, according to all the treatises on dance. (581)
Through the display of various [gestures], the heroes and yoginīs will be honored;
all the treatises on dance consist of the mudrās of performance and so forth. 581.
The mudrās of Śrī Heruka bestow all accomplishments; through the internal fire-offering (homa), there is the excellent worship of the Vīras and Devīs. 582.
That is the vastness of glorious Heruka, who perfectly bestows all siddhis;
through the inner nature of the fire offering, one should properly worship the heroes and goddesses. 582.
Through that which arises from the illustrious Saṃvara, the bestower of all accomplishments, the drinking of the moon becomes the mind’s eternal and supreme state. (583)
The glorious Cakrasaṃvara has truly arisen; he bestows all siddhis.
With a mind that has become the drink of peace, it is the state of supreme permanence. 583.
Furthermore, there was the drinking of soma juice, accompanied by wine, meat, and other such things. || 584 ||
The other peaceful drink is truly endowed with liquor, meat, and so forth. 584.
Oṃ sarvavajraḍākinī sarvabhakṣa śodhaye guhyaṃ vajriṇi hūṃ svāhā. (Mantra 60)
oṃ sarvabuddhaḍākinī sarvabhakṣaṇaśodhaya guhyavajriṇi hūṃ svāhā || mantra 60 ||
Having consecrated it with mantras, one should empower it. || 585 ||
Having praised it, he consecrated it. || 585 ||
Alternatively, having understood everything to have the form of the co-emergent (sahaja) through the yoga of eating and so forth,
one who is habituated to eating eats.
The wise yogi should not practice yoga. || 586 ||
Alternatively, the wise yogi, having recognized all food and so forth as the coemergent form, partakes of the meal with devotion. 586.
In the innate fire-pit of the belly, upon the eight-petaled navel-lotus, within the terrifying Heruka produced by passion, at the center of the pericarp,
the goddesses are seated with their expanded skulls fixed upon the certain petals.
Thereafter, in the triple circle (tritayacakra), which is provided with female gatekeepers (dvārapālī). || 587 ||

The innate belly is the hearth; the eight-petaled lotus at the navel is the face of Heruka, most terrifying, from which the bliss of the navel arises. Having certainly attained the lotus of the goddess, which is greatly enveloped by the petals—
Following that, it is endowed with the three wheels and the gatekeepers. || 587 ||

When the firewood of the *skandhas* is ignited by various kinds of offerings— such as the five nectars beginning with the glorious ten flavors— and by excellent, diverse sacrificial fuels, it becomes by its very nature a fire of omniscient wisdom that produces flavor in an instant.
Then, the master of mantras should perform the fire oblation there every day.
With various supreme oblation substances, such as the glorious nectar that opens up and bestows many diverse flavors,
[one offers] to the nature of the fire of omniscience, which blazes with the fuel of the aggregates and undergoes transformation in an instant.
A skilled mantrika should always perform these burnt offerings (homa) therein. 588.
And so it has been said:
"Likewise, it is taught:
'O Vajra, listen to the internal [practice]; in that manner, one should accomplish the fire offering (homa).'"
When it blazes with great splendor, one should offer oblations without conceptualization.
Listen, O Vajra, whose nature is internal! How is the fire offering perfectly accomplished?
One burns within the great blazing, majestic, and non-conceptual [fire]. 589.
The wise one should offer as oblations all food and drink whatsoever;
likewise, it is said that the five aggregates, beginning with form, are the sacrificial fuel (samidh). 590.
Whatever food and drink there may be, the wise should burn them all;
the fuel as it has been taught is the very nature of the aggregate of form and the rest. 590.
One should offer as the supreme restraint that mind which is free from conceptual construction;
likewise, semen, blood, flesh, feces, and urine constitute the fivefold [offering]. (591)
It is burned by non-conceptuality. Whatever is the nature of the mind consists of semen, blood, and likewise flesh, excrement, and urine as the fifth. 591.
The wise one, with a non-conceptual and essence-less mind, should consume the portion for the fire-oblation, as well as pride, aversion, and passion. (592)
One should consume [them] with non-conceptuality; by one possessing the wisdom that things lack intrinsic nature, so too are pride, delusion, hatred, and attachment [consumed]. 592.
Envy, avarice, and malice—these very things, when purified through the application of the intent toward the true reality, constitute the innate maṇḍala of the body. 593.
Envy and avarice are deceit; the observance of the commitments is stainless.
By uniting with that which is excellent in reality, the coemergent mandala of the body [is realized]. 593.
Whatever is to be offered as an oblation (balikriyā) and so forth within the circle of the body,
one should offer that oblation outside at night, having become naked and with the topknot loosened.
Whatever offerings there may be, such as the *bali*, one should perform the fire sacrifice within the mandala-circle of the body;
at night, with hair loosened and naked, one should offer the *bali* outside. 594.
Having gratified those of great splendor who stand upon the path with the previously described ritual by means of an offering, together with the yoginīs and vīras, || 595 ||
By means of the ritual previously taught, one abides on the path and possesses great majesty;
through the offering of the bali, one is pleased by the yoginīs and the heroes. 595.
Having ascertained the disposition of the sentient being, one should satisfy them with external homa;
it is stated in the Yoginītantra that the offering should be made within the maṇḍala of the body. (596)
In accordance with the inclinations of sentient beings, the external fire offering is explained;
as taught in the glorious Yoga Tantra, one should perform the fire offering within the mandala of the body. 596.
Since the body consists of the Buddha, one should perform the fire offering (homa) right there;
one should indeed cause the fire offering to be performed in the center of the lotus of the body, which is the support. || 597 ||
Because the Buddha is the body, by that samaya he is to be burned;
the support and the supported are the lotus, and within it the fire offering is to be performed. 597.
The nectar of the five meats is to be consumed together with the drinking of wine.
One should partake of meat and nectar, and properly consume liquor as well. 598
And so it has been said:
likewise, it is stated:
"Even though obstructed by the dense covering of the fuel of the aggregates..."
Impelled by the wind of compassion with the fires of primordial wisdom,
that pervasive Victor indeed smokes, blazes, and— once consumed by his own splendors— perceives the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). || 599 ||

Although the fuel of the aggregates is moistened and covered by obscurations, when fanned by the wind that produces gnosis-fire, it emits smoke and is consumed by the very flames of fire; pervasive and victorious, that is seen as the dharmadhātu. 599.
One should satisfy [the deity] by means of both the body-homa and the external homa;
relying upon the vajra-amṛta and other substances, one should perform the external homa. (600)
Possessing the fire sacrifice of the body, one pleases [the deities] with external fire sacrifices;
relying on vajra-amṛta and so forth, one should properly undertake the external fire sacrifice. 600.
The sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) should be one cubit in measure, beautiful in the shape of a skull;
likewise, it is perfected when surrounded by a triple enclosure, facing south, according to the prescribed rule.
The fire-pit shall be one cubit in measure, beautiful like a skull-cup;
facing south according to the ritual procedure, one succeeds by circumambulating while facing it. 601.
In the center, an eight-petaled lotus is situated upon the mountain;
on its petals are a battle-axe, a noose, and a trident together with a khaṭvāṅga staff. (602)
In the center, an eight-petaled lotus is well-situated upon the mountain;
upon the lotus are a sword, a noose, a spear, and likewise a khaṭvāṅga. 602.
One should place a vajra of a wrathful form, most terrifying, in the center;
on the outside, one should fashion a garland of vajras and a well-constructed altar in the shape of a lotus.
Extremely terrifying like a wrathful deity, one should place [the syllable] at the vajra-navel and form a vajra-garland on the exterior; the perimeter is excellent, like a lotus. 603.
Like the sacrificial ladle (śruva) and the large spoon (sruva), it is likewise the vessel for the Yoga Tantra;
however, one should draw two skull-like [faces] on the sides and the thunderbolt of wrath (krodhāśani) in the center.
The filling ladle and the pouring ladle of the Yoga Tantras are likewise;
their mouths are slightly shaped like skull-cups, and in the center, one should draw the vajra of the wrathful deity. 604.

Having uttered the *ālikāli* (vowels and consonants), the knower of the yoga of *saṃbhava* and the rest should offer the excellent substances for the fire sacrifice (*homa*) and so forth on the left, according to the left-hand practice (*vāmācāra*). || 605 ||
One should properly recite the *āli* and *kāli*; one should know the yogic sciences such as the source (*ākara*) and so forth.
With substances for the fire offering (*homa*) and the like on the left, one should perform the fire offering through the conduct of the left (*vāmācāra*). 605.

Having performed the worship according to the ritual procedure with the great mantras beginning with "Advaya," and having offered oblations into the fire for Śrī Heruka and the others, one should request the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
From the great tantras such as the *Advayavajra*, one should accept the offerings after performing the ritual of worship and the fire sacrifice (*homa*) for Agni, Śrī Heruka, and the others. 606.
One who knows the excellent yoga, desiring success, should perform a fire-oblation with the flesh of humans, cows, dogs, goats, sheep, horses, and elephants.
One who desires spiritual accomplishment should perform the fire offering with the flesh of humans, oxen, she-mules, jackals, horses, and elephants, according to the knowledge of yoga. 607.
Having loosened his topknot in secret and preceded by the consumption of naked sacrificial pap, the great yogin of the Śrīsaṃvara should commence the rite of fire-offering (homa). || 608 ||
With hair loosened and naked in secret, having previously practiced and partaken of food, the yogin of glorious Saṃvara should properly undertake the rite of the bali offering. 608.
The Ritual for Outer and Inner Fire Offerings. || o || Closing 11 ||
This is the ritual for the outer and inner fire offerings. Closer 11.
Accompanied by the yoginīs, the mantra-practitioner, facing south, should speak thus according to the ritual procedure to the disciples stationed at the southern side of the mandala.
The mantrin together with the yoginī, facing south and remaining within the mandala, should speak these words to the disciple according to the ritual procedure: 609.
O sons, you must indeed protect the excellent vow with great effort;
for there is nothing superior to the glorious Saṃvara, which is characterized by the innate means.
Therefore, through certain and diligent effort, you must guard the supreme vows.
There is no bliss higher than the glorious Cakrasaṃvara, which is characterized by the coemergent (*sahaja*). 610.
Furthermore, standing before the maṇḍala, you should speak again:
"The Mātṛkās and so forth, situated within the skull, destroy the impurities of the disciple. (611)
Having made the mandala the foremost, or else having spoken [thus], the skull-cup containing the mother and others serves to purify the sins of the disciple. || 611 ||
Holding [the vessel] with the left hand while recollecting the seven-syllable mantra, one should remain well-established with the pride of being Herukī-vīra. || 612 ||
Holding [the vessel] well with the left hand, recollecting the seven syllables, and focusing on the visualization of Heruka, one should remain perfectly poised with the sense of divine pride. 612.
The wise one gradually sprinkles the joys of all disciples, the kisses of Vārāhī, and the heart-powers of the Māras.
Kissing the Vajravārāhī, he who steals away the power and destroys the Māras from the mouths of all disciples was gradually cast down by the one of noble intelligence. 613.
Having performed the thorough protection of the Dharma with the great mantras beginning with the Six Heroes,
one should bind the headband upon the disciples, consecrated with the mantra of the Ḍākinīs.
Having performed the ritual actions with the mantras of the six sense faculties and so forth, one should thoroughly protect the disciple;
one should bind the silk streamers that have been consecrated with the mantra of the ḍākinīs. 614.
One should request the fee from the disciples, who are adorned with all ornaments, for they are the bestowers of joy upon living beings and the practitioners of all accomplishments. (615)
The disciple, adorned with all ornaments, makes the request from the south: "Grant the accomplishments to those beings who protect all accomplishments. (615)
Then the Guru, taking the disciple with his left hand and placing him at the southern gate, questions him in the Potaṅgi language.
Then, the master, always holding the disciple with his left hand, places him at the southern gate and questions him with the words of the *potaṅga*. 616.
The disciple should likewise speak in the *pratipotaṅgi* dialect, saying "O Lord!
Then the hero should cause him to recite the *gāyatrī* of Heruka. 617.
Then the disciple also spoke these words: "O Lord, pervasive one, Heruka, [please] smell the *gāya*! Thereupon, the Hero should speak. 617.
Oṃ, let us know Śrī Heruka; let us meditate upon the King of Vidyās; svāhā! Thus is the Gāyatrī. Mantra 61.
Oṃ śrī herukāya vidmahe vidyārājāya dhīmahi svāhā. This is the Gāyatrī. Mantra 61.
When this maṇḍala, the mistress of the ḍākinī network, has been accomplished,
you have been brought by me, O child, into the abode of Saṃvara.
In this mandala is the siddhi, the sovereign of the ḍākinī network; it is the foundation of Saṃvara—O son, you must take it up! 618.
At the southern gate, one should cause the disciple to recite;
at the southern entrance, the female disciple should utter this:
*oṃ namas te hūṃ namāmi hūṃ namo namaḥ hūṃ svāhā*. (Mantra 62)
Oṃ na ma te hūṃ | na ma mi hūṃ | na mo na ma hūṃ svāhā. Thus [it is said]. This is mantra 62.
One should perform three prostrations, distinguishing them as those directed toward Khecarī and the others;
having placed the joined palms upon the head, one should salute with the entire body.
The three prostrations are to be performed according to the specific distinctions such as the *khecarī* [and others].
Having placed the palms together at the crown of the head, one should prostrate with all limbs. 619 ||
Oṃ, to all the heroes and yoginīs, I offer myself as service for worship; may I be empowered by all the Tathāgatas, heroes, yoginīs, Ātma-Ḍākinī, and the rest. Mantra 63.
Oṃ, to all the heroic yoginīs who dwell in the cremation grounds, I offer myself; may you, the self-nature of all the Tathāgatas, the heroic yoginīs, and the ḍākinīs, establish me! Mantra 63.

Having caused [the disciple] to form the hollowed-añjali gesture at the heart with the left hand, one should cause the disciple—who is the abode of all virtues—to pay homage, beginning at the entrance. (620)
Joining the palms with the left hand at the heart, the disciple should prostrate at all the doors to that which has become the foundation of all qualities. 620.
Oṃ, I offer myself for the worship and empowerment of all heroes and yoginīs. May all the Tathāgatas, heroes, and yoginīs, beginning with Lāmā, empower me! (Mantra 64)
Oṃ, for the sake of the empowerment (*abhiṣeka*) of all the *vīrayoginīs*, I offer myself. May I be consecrated by the self-nature of all the Tathāgatas and *vīrayoginīs*. (Mantra 64)
Then, having again placed the left-hand añjali at the forehead, one should resort to the northern gate and pay homage to the Vīrayoginīs. 621.
Having placed the left palms against the forehead, one should then pay homage to the yoginīs while standing at the northern gate. 621.

Oṃ! To all the heroes and yoginīs, I offer this proceeding worship. O you who are identical with all the Tathāgatas, heroes, and yoginīs, beginning with Khaṇḍarohā, cause it to proceed for me! Mantra 65.

Oṃ, to all the Vīrayoginīs, I offer myself for the performance of worship. For the sake of the performance [of worship] for Khaṇḍarohā, the self of all the Tathāgatas and Vīrayoginīs, may they accept me! Mantra 65.
Then, having performed the *śikhāñjali* at the rear door,
the mantra-practitioner should worship the heroic Heruka preceded by the recitation of the mantra.
Then, from outside at the doorway, the mantrin, having joined his palms above his head, should first utter the secret mantra and pay homage to the Hero Heruka. 622.
Oṃ! In the rite of worship for all heroes and yoginīs, I offer myself; O you who embody the nature of all Tathāgatas, heroes, and yoginīs, beginning with Ādyā, perform the activity for me! Mantra 66.
Oṃ! May all the Vīrayoginīs purify my own actions through their own emergence. O you who possess the form of the Vīrayoginī of all the Tathāgatas, perform the rite for me! (Mantra 66)
The procedure for the four means of valid cognition. || 12 ||
This is the ritual of the four prostrations. Closer 12.
Having arrived at the southern gate and standing facing south, he takes the disciple with his left hand and bestows the supreme commitment (samvara). 623.
Having gone to the southern gate, one should stand well facing south; holding the disciple with the left hand, one should bestow the supreme vow. 623.
Go for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha—the Three Jewels. This is the firm vow within the delightful family of the Buddhas. 624.
I take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha—the Three Jewels. Herein, one enters the delightful Buddha-family and becomes firm in the vows. 624.
"O Mahāmati, you must take up the vajra, the bell, and the mudrā;
that which is the thought of awakening (bodhicitta) is the vajra, and wisdom is known as the bell. (625)
You of great intelligence should also grasp the mudrās of the vajra and the bell;
the bodhicitta is the vajra, and wisdom is called the bell. 625.
The teacher, a guru equal to all Buddhas, must be accepted by you.
This is called the commitment (*samvara*) and the pledge (*samaya*) when the Vajra family has been accomplished. (626)
O Master, you must uphold this; it is equal to all the Buddhas, the Gurus.
This is the purity of the Vajra family; it is called the vow and the commitment. 626.
The fourfold gift should be bestowed six times every day:
the gift of Dharma, the gift of material goods, the gift of fearlessness, and the gift of loving-kindness, always within the Jewel Family.
Within the Jewel Family, one should always, six times every day, bestow the four kinds of gifts: material wealth, fearlessness, the Dharma, and loving-kindness. 627.
And you must grasp the True Dharma—outer, secret, and pertaining to the three vehicles;
this is the supreme vow, the state of purity within the Lotus Family. 628.
You have upheld the sublime Dharma of the three vehicles—outer, inner, and secret. This is the supreme state of the vow of the pure Lotus family. 628.
I firmly accept the restraint associated with all [the families], performing acts of worship according to my ability within the exalted assembly of the great families of ritual action. 629.
I shall firmly and individually uphold all the vows; I shall also perform the rites of worship to the best of my ability. This is the eternal, great family of action. 629.
The Procedure for the Vow. || o || Closing 13 ||
This is the ritual for the vows. Closer 13.
Today you are established, O child, in the lineage that perceives reality, which has arisen from Vīradevī and is beautiful in the form of Heruka. (630)
May this being abide in its respective state; behold the reality of the family!
O Heroine, you have emerged well; you are as exceedingly beautiful as Heruka. 630.
That perfected knowledge of Heruka, by which the supreme state is attained when the void of space arises—that boon I shall grant to you. (631)
That which is generated is empty like space; you shall attain the supreme state.
O glorious Heruka, I bestow that supreme primordial wisdom upon you. 631.
"You must not speak to a person who has not seen the maṇḍala;
if you do speak, my child, you will destroy the samaya."
Do not speak of this to those who have not seen the mandala;
if you do speak of it, your samaya, my son, will be violated. 632.
Śrīvārāhī herself is now established within your heart;
she will depart at that very moment if you speak this rule. (633)
O glorious Vārāhī, this one who has truly entered your heart—if you speak of this method, he shall depart immediately after rending [your chest] asunder. 633.
Having recited the Ḍākinī mantra and chanting these words, one should cause the excellent disciple to drink the water of the five nectars from the vessel. (634)
One should give the vessel of water containing the five nectars to the supreme disciple; while reciting the mantra of the ḍākinī, these words should be spoken: 634.
This water of hell shall arise for you through the transgression of the samaya; but for those who guard the samaya, there is accomplishment—drink this water of the five nectars! 635.
"This is your hell-water; it will burn you if you transgress the samaya.
If you guard the samaya, accomplishments will come. Drink this water of the five nectars! (635)
Oṃ pañcāmṛtodaka ṭhaḥ hūṃ || Mantra 67 ||
oṃ paṃ tsa a ṃ r to da ka ṭha hūṃ || mantra 67 ||
From this day forward, I am your Śrīvārāhī; whatever I say must be performed by you with diligence, and I am not to be disregarded. 636.
From this day forward, I am your glorious Vārāhī;
therefore, you must strive to do whatever I say.
Do not treat me with contempt! 636.
Lest, by failing to avoid poison, you should meet your end and fall into hell—speak then! Let all the heroes and yoginīs remain present, and let Śrī Heruka and the others descend into me. 637.
"Lest you die without having abandoned your pride and fall into hell—O son, speak these words! Grant me your blessings, O heroes and yoginīs;
I pray that Śrī Heruka and the others descend upon me! (637)
Taking a cloth stained with blood, along with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and guggulu,
one should grind them together with māyārīviṣṭha and then consecrate them with mantras.
Having taken blood from the head, together with the five nectars, asafoetida, and cat excrement, one should perform the fumigation and offer praise. 638.
Having placed [the object] upon a lotus and thoroughly fumigated it with the fire of the funeral pyre,
one who is enraged and possesses a haughty mind should recite the mantra non-dually.
One should place [the substance] inside a skull-cup; it should be thoroughly fumigated with the fire of a cremated corpse.
With a mind that is wrathful and expanded, one should offer praise through non-duality. 639.
Then, having equipped him with the previously mentioned ornaments and likewise donned the armor, the wise one should again cause the entire wheel to enter the body of the disciple. (640)
Endowed with the ornaments previously taught, and likewise with the armor for the limbs, the wise one should again place all the wheels upon the body of the disciple. 640.
He gazes upon the disciple who has been entered [by the power], as the true wheel situated in the navel-lotus shines forth with rays, impelled by the downward-moving wind from the feet.
The excellent wheel situated at the navel lotus is luminous and radiant;
stirred by the wind beneath the feet, it is visualized as descending upon the disciple. 641.
Having recited the mantra of non-duality and assuming the ālīḍha posture, the wise practitioner should fumigate [the site] with the incense previously described. 642.
Recite the non-dual secret mantra while properly seated with the right leg extended; the wise one should perform the fumigation with the incenses previously described. 642.
Oṃ, abide, O Great Wrathful Incarnation, hūṃ! Oṃ, we know Śrī Heruka; we meditate upon the King of Vidyās, svāhā! (Mantra 68)
Oṃ tiṣṭha mahākrodhāveśa hūṃ | Oṃ śrīherukayabidmahe vidyārājāya dhīmahi svāhā || Mantra 68 ||
By this, the Hero has been impelled.
By saying this, he exhorts the hero.
One should open the eyes while they are held by his hand and draw them [toward him], saying:
"O Śrī Vārāhī, today you yourself are intent upon opening my eyes;
she opens every eye, the unsurpassed vajra-eye. (643)
Taking it from his hand with one’s own hand, one should open the eyes and show [the mandala]:
“O glorious Vārāhī, you must strive to open my eyes; may all eyes be opened—the unsurpassed vajra-eye. (643)
Oṃ vajranetrāya kara paṭala hrīḥ || Mantra 69 ||
Oṃ sarvabuddhaḍākinīye vajravarṇanīye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā || Mantra 69 ||
Behold this maṇḍala with the force of faith; born into the family by the wind, you have been empowered by the mudrās and mantras of the yoginīs. || 644 ||
By the power of your faith, look now upon this mandala!
You are born into the family of yoginīs, consecrated by mantra and mudrā. 644.
Having observed the flower that has been cast down, wherever it falls— whether upon a pedestal or another such place— therein shall success be attained.

Looking at the scattering of flowers, those who remain properly seated on their cushions and so forth—in whichever place the flower falls, for that person there shall be the attainment of siddhi. 645.
Some yogins maintain that the rite of external possession occurs externally; however, according to the doctrine of our teacher, possession arises within the [inner] seat of empowerment (sādhiṣṭhāna).
